paragraph: Old Tappan is a single-family town first, with 21 detached sales over six months at a median of $1,460,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00. About 48 percent sold above asking with a median of 28 days on market, which is competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes are moving, and sellers who aim high are generally okay with waiting for the right buyer. The range runs from $689,000 to $2,850,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Condos and townhouses are a thin slice here, 7 sales at a median of $870,000, with a ratio of 1.014 and a median of 14 days on market. Seven sales is too small to build a trend on, but they are clearly moving faster than the houses. Monthly counts are thin enough that no single month tells you much, though the single-family arc built from $1,200,000 in April to $1,736,250 in June before settling at $1,417,500 in July, which tracks the normal Bergen County summer peak. If the usual seasonal pattern holds, expect fall closings to ease off that June high.
